To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) prediction accuracy is a poor measure of the quality of the data, (2) there is a need for new measures that can be used to assess the quality of the anonymized data, and (3) we propose a methodology and three such measures.

(i) the accuracy of a classifier built from anonymized data is not a good measure of how well the data preserves the patterns that were in the original; (ii) there is a difference between the accuracy of a prediction made from anonymized data, and the accuracy of a pattern found in anonymized data; and (iii) we have designed a new methodology for evaluating the quality of modified data, and three new metrics for measuring aspects of data quality that no existing techniques can measure.
